one_star_reviews.text: The service at Tanguay and their repair partner, Atelier G Paquette, is seriously appalling. After three weeks without an oven—a 54-week-old oven, no less—and three visits from clueless technicians, our oven still doesn't work. Even worse, the last technician damaged our oven by repeatedly opening it and doing whatever he wanted. The result: a doubly broken oven, courtesy of Tanguay! Do yourselves a favor and go to Costco!

1. Purchased 5 appliances from Tanguay in the last year.

2. Had a stove completely burn out after 54 weeks on August 1st.

3. Spent hours on the phone only to be told by the employee that Tanguay always backs out once the due date has passed by even one day.

4. Be told by the Consumer Protection Office (OPC) that Tanguay is wrong, but that we have to prove it and fight for it.

5. Left a well-deserved bad review for Tanguay.

6. Be told to contact them at their social media email address.

7. Received no response.

8. Left more reviews.

9. Finally had a technician come to assess the situation. We had to argue that we wouldn't pay for the visit, and he agreed. He suggested we buy our future appliances at Costco. 10. Receive an email on Friday at 4:00 PM from supervisor Yann Gosselin asking for a phone number "to discuss it."

11. Reply within 30 minutes with the phone number on file.

12. Receive a call the following Monday, August 10th, from a woman named Josianne "who wants to resolve the problem and discuss it."

13. Start by resolving the problem. Article 38 of the Consumer Protection Act is clear, although it will be drastically strengthened in October 2026.

14. To be continued, we still don't have a working stove.

15. Josianne calls back to say "they managed to get the part for us free of charge."

16. The repair shop gives us an appointment. The technician shows up without calling ahead and asks us, "What's the problem?" Finally, he consults his documents and reports, finds the part diagnosed by the first technician, and comes to replace it.

17. The oven still doesn't work. He's switched between parts twice now, repeating that "it's weird." We'll see if we can get a working oven.

18. The second technician finally finds that the problem isn't the motherboard, but the connection to the motherboard.

19. They have to order the part.

August 15th, still no oven, we're waiting for their return.

August 21st, the technician is back with...the wrong wire. He realizes it after taking everything apart. He has to come back. Still no oven.

22. We realize that the technician bent the front control panel. Now we have an even more broken, non-functional oven.

Help yourselves, go to Costco...

Extremely disappointing experience with A1 Auto Depot.

I purchased a used fuse box from this business after being told it was the correct part for my vehicle. The part they sold me was not the correct part and did not match the original fuse box on the vehicle.

I completely understand that when purchasing used electrical parts, there is always a risk that the part itself may have an electrical problem. I was willing to accept that risk. But this wasn’t a case of a defective used part. They sold the wrong part.

When I returned and tried to resolve the issue, they refused to take the part back or even exchange it, saying it was a “final sale.” I asked to speak with the owner, and the person told me that he was the owner.

What bothered me even more than losing money on the wrong part was the way I was treated. Instead of trying to resolve a legitimate customer concern professionally, the owner raised his voice at me and called me a liar.

I run an automotive repair business myself, and I understand how used parts and final sales work. But selling a customer the wrong part and then refusing to exchange it is one thing; yelling at the customer and calling them a liar is completely unacceptable.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend A1 Auto Depot, especially to mechanics or shops relying on them to supply the correct parts. Verify everything yourself before paying, because if they give you the wrong part, you may be stuck with it.

I shopped at Staples on Sunday, and it was the worst experience I've ever had at any Staples location.
There were plenty of staff in the store, but it seemed no one was checking pricing or stocking items properly. I was looking for a school agenda for my son and found a Moleskine 2027 Weekly Planner (5" x 8.25") in the sale/clearance section with a label showing $17.97. I thought that was a great deal, so I took it to the cashier.
At checkout, I was told the price was $37.99. When I pointed out that the shelf label clearly showed $17.97, the response was basically, "You know it's an expensive planner. It's just in the wrong place." There were multiple planners displayed in that same section, not just one misplaced item. The employee took the planner from my hand and walked away without offering any further assistance.
I thought maybe that was an isolated mistake, so my son and I continued shopping. We then found a number of Cambridge journals/planners displayed together with a clearance tag of $7.99. Once again, when we got to the cashier, the price came up as $17.99. We received the same explanation: the items were supposedly in the wrong place.
I don't understand how multiple products can be displayed together under incorrect pricing and no one takes responsibility. Instead of checking the labels or acknowledging the issue, staff seemed to blame customers for picking up items where they were displayed. The way the products were handled felt dismissive and unprofessional.
This experience left me feeling frustrated and unwelcome. Accurate pricing and respectful customer service should be basic expectations. I will not be returning to this Staples location.
Would not recommend.

This was not just poor service; it showed a complete lack of respect, professionalism, and understanding toward customers and their religious practices.

Honestly, this experience was shocking. This is certainly not the kind of treatment I expected when I came to Canada. Management seriously needs to address the attitude and customer-service standards at this location.

I have never received such appalling and unprofessional service.

I had a central vacuum system installed in my home. During the installation, the homeowner came to my house and explained that, given the age of my house, it was absolutely necessary to install one outlet on the ground floor and another on the stairs, as there was no other option.

While I was downstairs with him, his colleague installed the outlet upstairs. When I came back up, I was shocked to find that the outlet had been installed directly in the middle of a step, not on the riser.

I was obviously very uncomfortable and expressed my astonishment. He replied that he had explained to me that the outlet would be on the stairs. This is false: he had simply told me that an outlet had to be installed "on the stairs." I obviously never imagined it would be placed right in the middle of a step, which is both unsightly and frankly impractical.

The most disappointing thing is that after that, he left quickly, leaving me to deal with the situation.

But the worst was yet to come. The outlet installed in the step was so tight that the hose barely fit, unlike the one on the ground floor. About six months later, the hose fitting broke, clearly due to this overly tight installation.

So I went back to see them with the hose. They called me back to tell me that the hose needed to be replaced. When I explained that the problem stemmed from the outlet installed in the step, the owner immediately raised his voice, saying, "You can't blame me for this!" I tried to calmly explain my point of view, but he ended the conversation by hanging up on me.

I find this way of treating a customer completely unacceptable. A problematic installation, a refusal to acknowledge the issue, and, most importantly, an aggressive and deeply unprofessional attitude when a legitimate question is raised.

I absolutely do not recommend this company.

I strongly recommend avoiding this Canada Post location.

I was with my friend while she attempted to complete a simple Amazon return. Her return instructions clearly stated that no additional packaging or label was required, but the employee refused to listen to her explanation. She repeatedly interrupted us, raised her voice and turned what should have been a straightforward transaction into an unnecessarily confrontational situation.

The employee also questioned why my friend had purchased and returned several items. This was inappropriate and completely unrelated to processing the return. A customer should not be interrogated or made to feel judged for using Amazon’s return service.

What was particularly concerning was the noticeable difference between how the employee treated us and how pleasantly and professionally she had treated the Caucasian customer immediately before us. As people of colour, we felt singled out by the sudden and drastic change in her behaviour, leaving us seriously concerned that racial bias may have influenced the interaction.

The most disturbing moment occurred when she repeatedly threw a package clearly marked “FRAGILE” across the counter. When we questioned her attitude and handling of the parcel, she became even more hostile, used inappropriate language and aggressively moved toward us in a physically intimidating manner.

The entire experience was upsetting, embarrassing and completely unnecessary. After all the commotion, which the employee created, she also failed to clearly confirm whether another package she had accepted was successfully processed. My friend was left having to contact Amazon customer service to determine what happened.

Customers should be able to complete a basic return without being interrupted, insulted, interrogated or intimidated. I sincerely hope management investigates this incident and reviews any available security footage. Based on what I personally witnessed, this was some of the worst and most concerning customer service I have ever experienced.

one_star_reviews.text:
I would give this Circle K  location ZERO stars if Google allowed it. This was one of the worst and most disrespectful customer-service experiences I have ever had.

I went into the store to purchase cigarettes and was asked for ID. No problem — I understand that employees are required to verify age. I actually had to walk all the way back outside to my car, get my ID, and come back inside specifically to show it to them.

After I handed the employee my ID, he looked at it and immediately told me that my ID was expired. The problem? It wasn’t expired at all — the expiration date clearly says 2027. He apparently couldn’t even read the expiration date correctly before accusing me of presenting an expired ID.

Instead of simply taking another moment to look at the ID carefully and correct the mistake, the situation turned into an embarrassing and disrespectful confrontation. After I had already gone outside to get the identification they requested, I was treated like I was the problem because an employee couldn’t properly read the date printed on my ID.

What made the experience even worse was the way we were treated afterward. I personally felt singled out, discriminated against, and that the treatment was racist. I cannot speak to what was in anyone else’s mind, but I can absolutely describe how their behavior made me feel.

There is nothing wrong with asking customers for ID when purchasing an age-restricted product. The problem is asking for ID, failing to read it correctly, incorrectly claiming that it is expired, and then treating the customer disrespectfully instead of simply double-checking your mistake.

If you’re responsible for selling age-restricted products, correctly reading identification is a basic part of the job. Customers should not be embarrassed, argued with, or kicked out because an employee makes a mistake reading an expiration date.

I hope the owner and Shell management take this seriously, review the security footage from the incident, and properly train the employees involved on ID verification, professionalism, discrimination, and basic respect for customers.

After the way I was treated here, I will never spend my money at this location again, and I cannot recommend this gas station to anyone.

Buyer Beware: I Specifically Asked About This Trap Before Buying

Mattress pricing is already a bit of a joke. Everything is somehow “$5,000” while simultaneously being on a miraculous 40–60% sale every other week.

So before buying from The Brick Mattress Store on Queensway, I specifically asked the manager what would happen if I needed to use the 90-day comfort exchange. My concern was very simple: **am I going to get trapped paying thousands more to switch mattresses because the promotional price changes?**

I was explicitly assured I would be taken care of.

He also told me he was throwing in roughly $600 of pillows/accessories for free. I bought over the phone and was never sent an invoice.

Now the mattress is too firm and I want the softer version. Thankfully, that mattress happens to be on one of these enormous sales right now for $2,999.

My current mattress is also selling for roughly $2,900.

Yet I’m being told I owe over $900 to exchange them because apparently my “free” accessories were actually billed at full price and my mattress was recorded as costing only around $2,000.

Think about that: the ONLY reason they aren’t asking me for thousands of dollars to use their “comfort exchange” is because the replacement mattress happens to be heavily discounted online right now.

That is exactly the scenario I warned them about before buying. I was assured it wouldn’t happen, trusted the manager’s word, and bought the mattress.

I’m happy to pay the actual ~$100 difference between the mattresses plus their $100 delivery fee. Not a cent more.

I’ve contacted the manager and will update this review if they honour what I was promised and make it right.

Until then, I’d strongly caution anyone shopping here to get absolutely everything in writing before relying on the 90-day comfort exchange.

I came in around 8:05 a.m. on 4th Sep., shortly after the store opened, and unfortunately had a very unpleasant experience.

I said “Good morning” three times as warmly and politely as I could, but the employee completely ignored me each time. While I was looking at the menu to decide what to order, she simply told me to “just wait” in a very curt and unfriendly tone.

I understand that mornings can be busy and that employees may need a moment to get things ready. If she had communicated that politely, I would have completely understood. However, her attitude made me feel as though having a customer come in at that time was an inconvenience to her.

It was only 8:05 a.m., but her attitude had already ruined my morning, so I decided not to order and left.

If the store opens at 8:00 a.m., I believe both the ingredients and the willingness to properly welcome and serve customers should be ready by then. A simple “Good morning, I’ll be with you in just a moment” would have made a huge difference.

The collection at the store is good, but unfortunately, the customer service was extremely disappointing.

We were trying to pay for our shoes and waited in line, but there was no proper queue system. Customers were being served randomly, which was already frustrating. When we politely asked the cashier, whose name I believe was nisha or aneesa , about our turn, she responded with a very rude and disrespectful attitude.

We explained to her that she could have spoken to us politely instead of being rude, but rather than acknowledging our concern, she became argumentative and insisted that what she was doing was correct. When I asked for her name  she properly spelled it for us and confidently told me to do whatever I wanted, which came across as extremely unprofessional and disrespectful.

Another staff member eventually came over and apologized to us, but the cashier simply stood in the corner, continued showing an unpleasant attitude, and appeared completely unconcerned about the situation.

As customers, we expect to be treated with basic respect and courtesy, regardless of whether we are making a purchase or asking a simple question. Unfortunately, this experience made us feel as though our business was not valued at all.

The products may be good, but customer service is equally important. I would strongly recommend that management look into this incident and provide appropriate training to staff on how to communicate respectfully with customers.

I had an extremely disappointing experience with the store manager, Zeenat, and will be escalating this directly to Shoppers Drug Mart.

I returned a product after specifically asking two employees, including Chris, what would happen to the PC Optimum points I had earned. I was told I could keep the value by receiving a gift card/exchanging for products of a similar value. Based on what the employees told me, I agreed to proceed with the return.

Zeenat then became involved, told me this was not possible, took back the products I had selected, and my points were also taken away. one_star_reviews.text:
I booked an appointment with BLS International in Vancouver for my passport renewal and travelled all the way from nanaimo to attend it. I took time off work, travelled approximately 3 hours, took the ferry, and spent over $300 on the trip, only to arrive and be told that their portal was down and they were unable to process applications.

What is even more frustrating is that there was no clear information about when the portal would be restored, and security (not even staff)could not even guarantee that it would be working on Monday. If the system is not functioning, why are appointments being allowed to remain booked without properly notifying applicants beforehand?

I understand that technical issues can happen, but what I found completely unacceptable was the way the situation was handled. The manager o any staff would not come downstairs to speak with the applicants, listen to their concerns, or provide any explanation or solution. Instead, security guards were sent to deal with frustrated customers. The security guard would not allow people to go upstairs to speak with management.

I have honestly never experienced a situation where customers who had travelled long distances, taken time off work, spent hundreds of dollars, and arrived for a confirmed appointment were simply left standing there without being given any meaningful assistance or accountability from management.

At the very least, management should have come down, addressed the applicants directly, explained the situation, and provided clear guidance on what we should do next. Customers should not have to chase management or argue with security guards just to have their concerns heard.

BLS International needs to understand that passport renewal is not a casual service for many people. People have travel plans, family emergencies, work commitments, and significant expenses involved. Taking appointments when your portal is not functioning and then providing no proper communication or solution is extremely frustrating and concerning.

BLS International, you should be ashamed of how this situation was handled. Technical problems can happen, but the lack of communication, accountability, and basic customer service is what made this experience unacceptable.

I sincerely hope BLS reviews how situations like this are handled and takes responsibility for ensuring that applicants are properly informed and supported instead of being left to deal with the consequences of BLS’s own system issues.

3. The blue handle shut-off valve was missing after installation. It was there before the installer arrived.

You may find unexpected residue or even missing parts in an appliance that is supposed to be new and unused.

1 star, terrible experience. No transparency, extremely unprofessional behavior, and I would not trust this company in my home again.

The technician came to fix one plumbing fixture. We were quoted approximately $300 for that repair and agreed.

While he was here, we asked him to look at a second fixture in the basement that we barely use. We specifically told him it was not urgent and asked him to confirm the additional cost before doing any work. We clearly explained that if it was around $100 extra, go ahead, but if it was going to double the bill, do not do it, our handyman was already coming the following week.

Instead, the technician went downstairs, came back a few minutes later and simply said it was done, and that the bill would now be roughly double. There was no price confirmation and no authorization from us for that amount.

The actual work on both fixtures appeared to take less than 10 minutes, yet the final bill was approximately $650.

What made the experience much worse was the technician’s behavior when we questioned the charge. Rather than calmly explaining what happened, the discussion became heated and he raised his voice inside our home to the point that our 2-year-old woke up frightened. Completely unacceptable behavior from someone entering a customer’s home.

We ultimately paid the bill, but the plumbing work took only a few minutes while the argument over the billing lasted much longer.

The issue isn’t simply that the service was expensive. It’s the lack of transparency and failure to get approval before performing additional work, followed by the way the situation was handled when we challenged it.

We also contacted the office and found them completely unhelpful in resolving the situation.

Based on our experience, I would never allow this company into our home again and cannot recommend them. When a customer specifically says, “Tell me the price before you do it,” that should be respected.

one_star_reviews.text:
My girlfriend and I recently went to the Edmonton Humane Society to adopt a cat, and unfortunately, what should have been an exciting experience turned into an incredibly disappointing one.

We instantly fell in love with a cat and went to the front desk to let the staff know we were interested. We were told that another person was also interested, but that they would call them to see if they were still interested. We waited on the bench, and a few minutes later, the staff came back and told us that the other person was no longer interested.

Based on that information, we filled out the adoption application and confirmed a pickup time for the following day. We were so excited that we spent the whole day purchasing all of the necessary supplies to bring our new cat home.

A few hours later, however, we received a call telling us that someone else would be receiving the cat because of a filing issue on the Humane Society's end.

We drove back to the center hoping there was some way to resolve the situation. After speaking with staff, we were told that we had done nothing wrong and that the issue was entirely due to their failure to file the correct paperwork. Unfortunately, that mistake resulted in us losing the cat we had already been approved to adopt and had prepared to bring home.

What makes this even more frustrating is that, after reading previous reviews, it appears that similar issues have been reported by other people before. If this is a recurring problem, it is extremely concerning that it has not been addressed.

We understand that animals need to be placed appropriately and that mistakes can happen, but this was a preventable administrative error that caused a lot of unnecessary disappointment, wasted time, and expense.

I genuinely hope the Edmonton Humane Society takes this seriously, reviews what happened, and makes changes so another family doesn't have to go through the same experience. This was an absolutely terrible adoption experience.

A manager’s role is to de-escalate situations and retain customers, not to talk down to them while ignoring their own store's organizational failures. one_star_reviews.text:
This was the first time I had ever taken my car to be professionally detailed. The detailing work itself was good. Unfortunately, the way a small concern was handled has left me questioning how a more serious issue would be addressed.

After my vehicle was cleaned, the black lug-bolt covers were missing from one wheel and put into my personal items box, all but one (the lock nut cover). I believe all five were present when I dropped it off, and portions of the footage appear to show them still in place. I have a video, which I provided of that tire with all the covers in place but it was from earlier in the summer, it’s the most recent one I had. That didn’t matter to Alex (the owner). I reached out to the Tech that cleaned me car and he stated “I asked the guys and they said they only pulled out 4 of the plastic caps, I took a look around the shop and I haven’t seen it anywhere”. Alex originally told me the video showed the car had arrived without those covers on at all. He sent me the video, however, the images are not perfectly clear, so I am including the available photos and videos and will let others draw their own conclusions.

From the beginning, I made it clear that I was not asking for a refund, compensation, or even the cost of a replacement. Volkswagen had already replaced the missing part for me free of charge after I explained what had happened. VW also let me know that it is usually a replacement fee of $80 because it was the Lug Nut cap that goes onto the Lock Nut, which you have to buy as a pair with a new lock nut. I was simply letting the business know what appeared to have happened.

The owner insisted that the video footage would clear everything up, even after I said I did not need to see it. When the footage was reviewed, it was inconclusive at best. The owner ultimately acknowledged that the photos and videos did not provide a clear picture, while also maintaining that the video proved no employee had “pulled” the covers off.

I had never accused anyone of deliberately pulling them off. My concern was that they may have been unintentionally dislodged during the cleaning, which the footage does not rule out.

When you pay for professional detailing, you are paying for attention to detail, no pun intended. Mistakes can happen, and this was a very small issue that cost me nothing. What mattered was how it was handled. Instead of simply acknowledging the possibility and treating the concern fairly, the response felt defensive and more focused on disproving responsibility than listening to a customer.

If this much resistance arises over something so minor, where no compensation was even requested, it naturally raises concerns about how a larger or more expensive issue might be handled with a much more valuable car. The cleaning work was good, but the lack of accountability in this situation means I will not return or recommend the business.

I would also suggest that prospective customers read through some of the other reviews. Based on what others have written, it appears I may not be the only customer with concerns about how an issue was handled when something went wrong. If you do choose to go here I would STRONGLY urge you to take photos and videos when your car is on the lot and have Alex himself come out and acknowledge the condition your car is in.

I found this shop on Google due to their marketing push last year (so if you find them on Google, be warned!). I rarely leave negative reviews, but unfortunately feel the need to warn others.

I tried on wedding dresses here. The experience was fine! the dresses are pretty, but their sizing runs very small, which detracted from the experience and ultimately led me not to buy my dress there. You are also NOT ALLOWED TO TAKE PICTURES. When asked why, we were told there could be cheap knock-offs made online if we took photos. Fine, I could maybe accept that… if it wasn’t for the fact that there are photos of ALL THEIR DRESSES ON THEIR WEBSITE?!
I went to at least 4 or 5 other bridal boutiques and everywhere let me take photos. Asking brides to spend thousands of dollars on dresses where you can’t take photos, is ridiculous in this day and age.

This is all not including my mom’s experience, who bought a dress here for my wedding. Natalia assured us personally that we could change her sizing if needed, and a new size could be ordered & delivered within 3 weeks. She said to come back in the summer leading up to my wedding.
Lo and behold, this was a lie.
We did as instructed, repeatedly following up to ensure my mom could get the right size prior to the wedding.
The conclusion? It would take 3 months to order a new one, and there was nothing they could do. So now my mom will need to spend 500$+ to resize her 1000$ dress, thanks to Natalia and her team lying to us.

It’s heartbreaking, because it’s a beautiful dress, now tainted by the stress and confusion caused by this store.

I would not trust anything this shop tells you, as many other reviewers confirm.

It’s too bad because their dress selection is lovely. But their customer service is unaccountable.

To any brides to be: I recommend La Jolie Robe. I know 4 other brides who also found their dresses there in 2025/26.

Best of luck!

I was about to leave all the items I had picked out. Luckily, there was a male employee at the checkout next to me helping another i customer. I asked him if he could
please check whether my payment had gone through. He checked it for me and said, “OK,” so I finally felt comfortable leaving.

Honestly, I don’t understand what those other employees were trying to prove. If they saw that a tourist was struggling with the language and having trouble with the payment machine, a little help and a clear explanation would have made everything much easier.

Traveling in another country is already difficult when you don’t speak the language well. I just hope staff can be a little more understanding and helpful toward customers. 🙏

one_star_reviews.text:
We purchased a stairlift from Silver Cross in London, Ontario, for my grandmother in February 2023. Over the three years she had it, the unit failed on at least four separate occasions, requiring paid service calls each time.
By December 2025—less than three years after installation—the main control box assembly failed alongside the battery, resulting in an $1,100+ repair bill ($828 for the control box, $150 for batteries, plus service). For a relatively new, premium mobility product, experiencing critical electronic failure this early was very odd.
The breaking point occurred in August 2026 when the unit broke down yet again. We reached out to their office at least three times seeking repair service and never received a single answer or callback. Leaving an elderly customer stranded without accessible mobility or even the courtesy of a response is inexcusable.
We ultimately hired an entirely different mobility company to remove the Silver Cross unit and install a reliable lift. Given the repeated equipment failures, high repair expenses, and complete absence of customer support when it mattered most, I strongly advise looking elsewhere.

I left Fabricland today feeling quite disappointed by an experience that should have been very simple.
I was purchasing some flannelette to make neckerchiefs for my son and noticed two identical totes, one green and one red, sitting together on a table clearly marked “Blowout Sale – $60.” I picked up the green one and asked the employee whether, with my Fabricland card, the price would be $60 or whether there would be an additional discount.
The employee looked at the tag on the tote and told me it was $69. I pointed out that the $60 sale sign was displayed directly with the two totes. Rather than honouring the clearly displayed sale price, the employees began comparing product numbers and determined that the bags had different numbers, so they would not honour the $60 price.
I understand that different products can have different SKUs, but from a customer's perspective, these two identical bags were together on a table under a very clear $60 Blowout Sale sign. If the sign was not intended to apply to the green bag, then the merchandise should have been clearly separated or the signage corrected.
What disappointed me most was not the $9 difference—it was the refusal to acknowledge how misleading the display was and the lack of willingness to find a reasonable solution.
I have shopped at Fabricland before, but experiences like this make a customer think twice about returning. I hope management will review how sale signage is being used in the store so that customers aren't left wondering which price they are actually expected to pay.

My wife booked an 8:30 AM appointment for an oil change. When I arrived at 8:30 to drop off the vehicle, the staff seemed surprised that I was there. They did take the keys and assured me the vehicle would be ready within 45 minutes to an hour.

I told them I would ride my bike back home and asked them to call me when the vehicle was ready. After an hour passed without receiving a call, I rode my bike back to pick it up, only to be told that they hadn’t even started working on it yet.

I was then told it would take another 30 to 45 minutes and that it would definitely be ready. I gave them more than another hour and rode back again. I tried calling before leaving, but no one answered the phone. When I arrived, my vehicle was still not finished.

I genuinely like supporting local businesses, and this location would have been very convenient for servicing our vehicles. Unfortunately, after being given multiple assurances about the timing and having to make several unnecessary trips by bike, I won’t be returning due to the lack of timely service and communication.

one_star_reviews.text:
I had a really bad experience with the cashier just a few minutes ago. My girlfriend and I (we're both 20) went to this convenience store intending to buy alcohol. Neither of us had ever bought alcohol before, so we weren't aware that it was illegal to sell it after a certain hour. That was our mistake, and we take full responsibility; that's not what bothered me. What deeply disturbed us was the cashier's attitude and the way he made it clear and treated us. As we were about to leave the refrigerated section and go to the register, the man came up to us and stared at us for several long seconds. After a moment of silence, we asked him if we could help him with anything. He immediately replied, "Do you think I'm an idiot?" Confused, we replied that of course not, and asked him why he was staring at us like that. He then said, "What do you have in your hands?" to which we replied, confused, "Alcohol." He said, "Do you know what time it is?" "Yes, it's midnight." After a silence and an indignant look from him, I realized he probably didn't have the right to sell it to us and I replied, "Oh, sorry, you don't have the right to sell it to us?" He started raising his voice and said, "Do you think I don't know what you came here for?" We said, "Sir, we came to buy it, sorry, we didn't know," and I put the cans down. He insisted he wanted us to leave the convenience store, so we did, and as I walked away, he asked me what was in my bag. I showed him the contents and offered to search them, which he refused. He started shouting and telling us we were going to receive a "message about this," that he wanted us to "get out," and that he never wanted to see us there again. I calmly offered to give the man my name and show him my ID, in case he wanted to file a theft report. He refused and told me to "get out," slamming the door shut.

What upsets me isn't that he didn't sell me alcohol. On the contrary, I think that's perfectly normal, and I should have checked before wanting to buy any at that time. However, I find it insulting, unjustified, and completely inappropriate to have treated us that way. Honestly, when he started swearing and raising his voice, we were scared. I understand that the man was asleep, that he may have woken up on the wrong side of the bed, and that there had probably been thefts before, but he absolutely had no right to treat us that way. I would suggest the manager or owner review the security cameras, because my girlfriend and I had no intention of stealing, and that's not at all what happened. I would also suggest the owner review with his employees how they treat their customers, because regardless of the time of day, everyone deserves to be treated with respect. Furthermore, we later went to another nearby convenience store to confirm what we had concluded, and the cashier kindly informed us that it was illegal after 11 p.m. In short, now we know, but it just goes to show that it is possible to answer customers' questions politely and calmly. Thank you.

As I was asked to leave a review, here is my honest experience with Windshield Surgeons South Edmonton.
I have previously taken my Sonata to another Edmonton location and had nothing but great things to say about them. They were professional, clean, and I was very happy with the service. Unfortunately, I can't say the same about my experience at the south-side location.
When I arrived, I was given the price for the windshield, which I had no issue with. I was also told there could be an additional charge of almost $40 for new molding if it was needed. I happened to be sitting where I could watch the work being done, and when the existing molding was removed, there didn't appear to be much effort made to preserve it. An end was grabbed and it was essentially yanked off. The $40 itself isn't a huge concern, but if replacing the molding is effectively standard procedure, I would rather simply be told upfront that it's part of the cost instead of being told it will only be charged "if needed."
What bothered me more was the level of professionalism. At one point I came around the corner and saw a female employee playfully holding my passenger door shut while a male employee was inside my truck, essentially preventing him from getting out. They may have just been joking around with each other, but when it's happening with a customer's vehicle, it doesn't come across as particularly professional.
After the work was completed, I paid and went outside to find my truck parked with the engine off but the transmission still in Drive.
Then I got inside. I understand this is a 20-year-old work truck, and I'm certainly not expecting anyone to detail it. However, I know the condition it was in when I dropped it off. There was grit, dirt and debris from the windshield removal left across my dash and center console. When you're paying for a professional service, I don't think it's unreasonable to expect the mess created during that service to be cleaned up. Even a quick vacuum or wipe-down would have made a significant difference.
The windshield itself may be fine, but the overall experience left me disappointed. Between the additional molding charge, the conduct around my vehicle, finding the truck left in Drive, and the mess left inside, I expected a more professional level of service.
Based on this experience, I probably will not return to the South Edmonton location. My experience at the other Edmonton location was considerably better.

My experience with Shoppers Drug Mart at Main and Danforth has left me extremely concerned about patient safety and accountability.

I gave my mother’s prescription to the pharmacy on August 25, 2026, giving them 10 days before her eye surgery on September 4 at 11:00 a.m. The eye drops needed to be started two days before surgery, and I clearly explained to the pharmacy that this medication was extremely important and time-sensitive.

Despite having more than enough time to prepare and arrange delivery, my mother never received the medication.

I also received pharmacy text messages indicating that the prescription was ready and/or delivered, so I reasonably believed that she had received it. On Wednesday at approximately 6:30 p.m., I discovered that she had never received the medication. I immediately contacted the pharmacy and was given multiple explanations rather than a clear answer and immediate resolution.

This is the third time we have experienced problems with medication delivery from this pharmacy. This time was particularly serious because the medication was required before surgery. My mother also has a heart condition, making proper medication management especially important.

What concerns me most is the apparent lack of accountability. When a pharmacy knows that a medication is time-sensitive and connected to surgery, there should be systems in place to ensure the patient actually receives it. If there is a delivery problem, the patient should be contacted immediately—not left to discover the problem themselves.

Based on this experience, I have serious concerns about whether this pharmacy is providing the level of care and accountability that patients should be able to expect. A failure involving essential medication could potentially have serious consequences for a patient.

I strongly urge management to investigate what happened, review the prescription and delivery records, and explain why the medication was not received despite the notifications we were given.

I hope management takes this feedback seriously and reviews what happened so that other customers do not have to go through a similar experience.

If you decide to work through this agency, do so at your own risk.

I am writing regarding an incident that occurred on a Saturday morning in 1st of August when I came to the station to fuel my vehicle.

I set the pump to run automatically and then sat in my vehicle while the fuel was dispensing. The amount had reached approximately $15 when the pump suddenly stopped, and the display showed “Pump Unavailable.”

I tried to restart the pump, but it would not work. I went inside and spoke with the cashier, Sukh, who told me that the pump was shut off for safety reasons because I was sitting in my vehicle while fueling.

I understand and respect legitimate safety policies, but I find this confusing because I regularly use other stations under the same brand (Petro Canada) and have sat in my vehicle while the fuel was dispensing. At those locations, the pump has never been stopped or made unavailable because I was sitting in my vehicle.

This is not an isolated incident at this particular location. It has happened to me multiple times, which is why I stopped coming to this station for a period of time.

I also want to mention that Sukh and I have had some personal issues outside of the workplace. However, I believe personal matters should remain separate from the workplace and should not affect how a customer is treated. Regardless of anyone’s personal feelings, the workplace should remain professional, and every customer should be treated fairly and respectfully.

I would like to speak directly with the manager about this situation, understand the station’s actual policy regarding customers remaining in their vehicles while fueling, and discuss why my pump has been repeatedly stopped or made unavailable.

Please let me know your availability, and I would be happy to meet and discuss this issue. Since this has happened multiple times, I would appreciate the matter being taken seriously. If I am unable to get a satisfactory resolution, I will consider escalating the complaint further.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointing experience at Ribouldingue, especially considering this is supposed to be a store welcoming to children and families.
I was there with my partner and our 1-year-old son. Our son was interested in the train table and the little cars, as you would expect from a baby in a toy store. He was supervised the entire time and was not breaking, throwing, or damaging anything.
An employee named Alain came over and started telling our 1-year-old “no, no,” because he apparently didn't want him playing with the cars on the train table. What I found particularly uncomfortable was that instead of speaking to us, the parents, he was repeatedly addressing our baby directly and even extending his hand toward him asking for the toy back.
I came back over and let my son play a little with the train set. Alain then returned AGAIN and once again started telling my son “no, no.”
At that point, I asked him why he kept doing this. His explanation was that my son “might” break something or that the car “might” scratch something.
I told him that my son wasn't doing either of those things, because he wasn't.
I completely understand that employees have a responsibility to protect merchandise. If my child were actually damaging something, I would immediately intervene. But there is a big difference between stopping a child who is damaging merchandise and repeatedly hovering over a supervised 1-year-old because of something he MIGHT do.
What made the experience particularly upsetting for me as a mother was watching an adult repeatedly approach my baby and tell him “no, no” when he wasn't doing anything wrong. He became visibly uncomfortable. At one year old, he obviously doesn't understand concerns about scratching a display or store merchandise. If Alain had a concern, he could simply have spoken respectfully to me or my partner and allowed us to handle our own child.
Instead, we were made to feel as though our baby wasn't welcome to touch or explore the toys in a toy store.
After the second interaction, we decided we didn't want to stay somewhere our child was being made to feel uncomfortable, so we left.
I rarely feel the need to write reviews like this, but this experience genuinely bothered me. A children's toy store should understand how to interact appropriately with very young children and, more importantly, how to communicate concerns respectfully to their parents.
Unfortunately, after the way Alain treated our 1-year-old, I would not feel comfortable bringing my son back here.

I had an extremely disappointing and uncomfortable experience at Ribouldingue because of the way an employee named Alain interacted with our 1-year-old son.

Our son was playing with some toy cars around the train table while we were right there supervising him. Alain came over and repeatedly told our ONE-YEAR-OLD “no, no,” insisting that he couldn't play with the cars on the train table because he might scratch or damage it.

What bothered us most was the way the situation was handled. Instead of simply speaking to us as the parents and politely explaining whatever rule the store has, Alain repeatedly addressed our baby directly and made him visibly uncomfortable. At one point, he even came close and extended his hand toward our son asking him to give the toy car back.

You would think that after expressing his concern once, that would have been the end of it. It wasn't.

When my partner came back and let our son play a little more with the train set, Alain came back AGAIN and started telling our son “no, no” for a second time. When my partner finally asked him why he kept doing this, Alain said that our baby might break or scratch something. My partner pointed out that our son wasn't breaking or scratching anything—and he wasn't.

This is a TOY STORE. Children are naturally going to be interested in toys, especially when there is a train table/display accessible to them. Obviously, parents should supervise their children and prevent them from damaging merchandise, and we were doing exactly that. If there is a specific rule about which toys can be used on the train table, then communicate that politely to the parents. There was absolutely no need to repeatedly hover around a 1-year-old, tell him “no, no,” and reach toward him for a toy when he wasn't damaging anything.

The whole interaction made us feel as though our son was being treated like a problem simply for behaving like a normal curious one-year-old in a toy store.

After Alain approached him yet again, we had had enough. We simply left.

We came into a children's toy store expecting a welcoming environment where families and young children would feel comfortable. Instead, we left because an employee's repeated behavior made our baby and us feel unwelcome.

Parents of babies and toddlers should know about our experience before deciding whether this is the environment where they want to bring their children.

I hope Chef Works takes the quality issue seriously and improves how these situations are handled.

one_star_reviews.text:
An honest review 1 year post-repair: good from far, far from good.

I worked for a company that outsources their services and I had seen very good work from their company. Eventually, I trusted this company enough to get a quote to repair some rust and perform a complete paint job. I got the quote, approved the work and within the same day they started the repairs. Everything was great. Constant updates, they let me know before going further it would cost more due to the severity, no problem. I was given a deadline of 3 months to complete

A few months go by… I’m not bugging them every day! Sometimes during lunch break I would inspect the car during its procedure. Note at this time the panel I provided them was self tapped into the body and all doors were removed. Every day I saw this car, it was parked outside. I understand! They have busy schedules and this was a cash side job.

Another month goes by, no progress has been made. At this point, it’s been sitting outside every day, already prepped for paint just waiting. I’m getting slightly concerned as it is now past the expected completion time. I still trust these guys because we work so close together and I’m still bringing them at least 2-3 customers a week.

Another month goes by and I get a call. “Hey, did your sunroof work before dropping it off?” Weird - yes of course it did. “Your cluster is not working as well, the car ran out of gas and we had to figure out how to fill it up”. Mind you at this point I was aware they were given this car with a full tank and everything still operational.

They paint the car, another month goes by. Apparently there were several electrical issues caused by a reverse-boost battery situation. They replaced my battery for me (the battery I had in the car was 1 year old) and said they checked the fuses and they were all good. (Later found out this was not true and they were lazy)

I called the owner. The owner straight up lied to me saying my car has been in the shop the whole time and is very protected. He did not know that I knew that was a lie. Keep in mind it is not fully confirmed but one of my coworkers saw my car outside when all the panels were off and it was raining and the interior was soaked.

One of the problem people I was dealing with (liar and super shady) had gotten fired then rehired the next week!!! This was my exhaustion point.

4 months after the original drop off day ( from May to September) I finally got my car back - electrical issues unresolved and immediate paint defects that were refused to be repaired as I had gotten a great discount. (Let’s keep in mind I was told every customer was a cash incentive I was supposed to get, I did not receive a single dollar. I was told this would help with a discount at the end of the paint job)

Another 6 months go by and I’m finally ready to have it out for the season as it is not winter driven and needed mechanical work. I took it to the owner who did not want to listen to my concerns and brushed me off saying there’s nothing he can do, he doesn’t have the paint code, and he refused to do any further work on my car.

Honest opinion: NEVER bring your car to this place. I have another repair shop that has already fixed a part of my car and will be slowly fixing the fuck ups this shithole of a company did.

I do not care how bad this looks on them, I was done dirty. I chose to stay quiet in hopes they would own up to their mistake; they chose not to.

I am writing to formally express my dissatisfaction with the ear piercing service my 5-year-old daughter received at this location in the Chinook Mall on Aug.24th, 2026. This was supposed to be a very special milestone, but the experience was deeply disappointing due to a lack of professionalism that caused me unnecessary stress.
Before the piercing, we took extra time to ensure the pre-marked spots were symmetrical and correctly placed. Despite this, one of the piercers completely missed the mark on my daughter's right ear. As a result, the earring sits noticeably different than the one on the left.
When I brought this to the manager's attention, she was dismissive. She stated it was not worth moving the piercing because she felt it was not noticeable, and she insisted they were symmetrical in height, and said they would still sit differently due to my daughter's ears themselves not being the same.
How can it be acceptable that the piercing was clearly not pierced on the mark that we agreed upon? Extremely frustrating and disappointing for the lack of care and attention that was put into my child's service.
I paid $95 for a service that was not performed correctly. It is unacceptable that the piercer completely missed the pre-marked spot that I had approved. No apology was given, and no refund was offered. Instead they just tried to convince me that everything was fine.

MetCredit is one of the worst companies I have ever had to deal with. My experience has been extremely frustrating and raises serious concerns about their transparency, accountability, and respect for consumer rights.

Reporting a balance of $34,275 when, according to my records, the original outstanding amount never exceeded $5,000 is absolutely unacceptable. I have been left questioning how such an extraordinary amount could possibly be justified.

This situation raises serious concerns about whether proper legal and consumer protection requirements are being followed. A debt collection company should not expect people to accept unexplained amounts without clear evidence and proper documentation.

In my opinion, the way this matter has been handled is disgraceful. I expect transparency, accountability, and a documented explanation—not an outrageous balance with unanswered questions.

**Based on my experience, I would not recommend MetCredit to anyone.** Consumers deserve fair treatment, honest communication, and respect for their legal rights. I intend to pursue this matter through the appropriate complaint channels until I receive a satisfactory explanation.

one_star_reviews.text: My dad and I went to this Aritzia yesterday (August 24, 2026). I went to go buy a pair of socks for back to school, however, the size and colour that I was looking for wasn’t available. As my dad and I tried to search for a staff member to help us out, we spotted literally no one. Not once did anyone ask us for help or support. Then, we decided to wait in line to ask one of the staff members at cash if they had the socks that I was looking for at the back. I thought that one of the employee was available to take the next customer in line, so both of us decided to go there and ask her. As I approached her, she gave me the weirdest eye contact, which made me feel really uncomfortable. However, she was still helping her other customer out. I’ll admit that it was our fault that we went even though she was still cashing out the other customer. I had no intention of going there to interrupt, but I seriously thought she was available. She sent as back at the line, which was valid. When she called us again, she and another employee were still giving us weird eye staring and rolls, and it really sounded as if she didn’t want to help us out. They treated us as if we were outsiders. Her interaction with the customer she was helping out before seemed so genuine and sweet, and the moment she started helping me, she was treating us like she didn’t want to in the first place, which is completely disrespectful. I also work in the retail industry, where customer service is extremely valued for every single customer, no matter the skin colour, attitude, etc. I suggest that before Aritzia drops new items and such, that the first review their process of hiring employees that actually treat every customer with respect. By the way, they were two Caucasian young girls, in the middle of the cashing area. This seriously needs to be addressed, as I have read so many more comments regarding micro-racism comments and such that have occurred at this place.

I’m disappointed with my experience here, particularly with the customer service.

During my previous rental, I had a bad experience because the vehicle I received had dog hair inside, and the interaction with the front desk at that time was not very pleasant. I was then told that they only keep their records for one year and that they could no longer find any information about what had been promised to me. What frustrated me most was the customer service. I spent around half an hour trying to explain the situation, but instead of trying to understand my point of view or find a reasonable solution, I felt like the conversation was mostly focused on explaining why they couldn’t help me.

I was actually prepared to rent a vehicle today, even aside from the free day, but the staff said they didn’t have the authority to book the rental and told me to go online to make the reservation.

I understand that businesses have policies about how long records are kept, but if a customer is promised something with no stated expiry date, there should be a way to document and honour that commitment. A little more effort to understand the situation and find a solution would have made a big difference.

Unfortunately, the overall experience left me feeling that customer service and communication could be significantly improved.

one_star_reviews.text:
⭐️ Really disappointed with my experience in Structube

I bought a dresser from Structube in 2023, and honestly, I never expected to be dealing with this after just a few years. Over the past year, the drawers kept getting loose, the slides started breaking, and eventually one of the drawers actually fell off.

I went to the Richmond Hill store, not to ask for a free replacement or to argue about the warranty. I simply wanted to know if there was anything I could do to fix it — maybe get replacement slides or spare parts, or find out if Structube had any kind of repair service.

Unfortunately, the response I got was basically, “That model is discontinued, the warranty is only one year, and there’s nothing we can do.”

I understand that the warranty has expired. What really bothered me was the lack of willingness to help. I was hoping someone would at least try to point me in the right direction or suggest a solution.

I honestly believe furniture should last more than two or three years, and even when something is out of warranty, I think a company should care about helping a customer keep a product they purchased from them in good condition.

I left the store feeling pretty disappointed. It wasn’t even about getting something for free  I just wanted someone to care enough to help.

Based on this experience, I’m unfortunately very disappointed with Structube
and will think twice before purchasing furniture from them again.
